Remark
[Polarization of algebraic curvature tensors]

Source: petersen:page-0130, petersen:page-0131 ↗ lem:pet-ch3-bivector-jacobi-identity ↗ prop:pet-ch3-curvature-symmetries

1. ch3:3.4.29Assume $R(X,Y,Z,W)$ is an algebraic curvature tensor, i.e. satisfies properties (1)--(3) of subsection 1.1. (1) Show \begin{align*} 6R(X,Y,V,W)& =\frac{\partial ^2}{\partial s\, \partial t}R(X+sW,Y+tV,Y+tW,X+sW)\Big|_{s=t=0}\\ & \quad -\frac{\partial ^2}{\partial s\, \partial t}R(X+sV,Y+tW,Y+tW,X+sV)\Big|_{s=t=0}. \end{align*} (2) Show $6R(X,Y,V,W)$ equals the explicit sum-of-twelve-terms expansion \begin{align*} & R(X+W,Y+V,Y+V,X+W)-R(X,Y+V,Y+V,X)-R(W,Y+V,Y+V,W)\\ & \quad -R(X+W,V,V,X+W)-R(X+W,Y,Y,X+W)+R(X,V,V,X)+R(W,V,V,W)\\ & \quad +R(X,Y,Y,X)+R(W,Y,Y,W)-R(X+V,Y+W,Y+W,X+V)\\ & \quad +R(X,Y+W,Y+W,X)+R(V,Y+W,Y+W,V)+R(X+V,Y,Y,X+V)+R(X+V,W,W,X+V)\\ & \quad -R(X,Y,Y,X)-R(V,Y,Y,V)-R(X,W,W,X)-R(V,W,W,V) \end{align*} (four terms are redundant, obtainable from polarizing $R(X,Y,Y,X)$).
